bus_service.title: Bus stops — scheduled service on 26 October 2026
bus_service.source: Stop-level service summary supplied by the user (granada_bus_frequency_2026-10-26.geojson), derived from a published timetable (GTFS); original feed and licence not stated in the file + outside the Granada municipality: Consorcio de Transporte Metropolitano del Área de Granada — lines, their stops and timetables from the open CTAN API (api.ctan.es), read 2026-11-23 (src = ctan)
bus_service.license: not stated in the supplied file — published at the user's request; confirm the GTFS licence

fields.trips_day: scheduled departures at the stop on the service date
fields.trips_7_9: scheduled departures in the window named "7_9" (07:00–09:00 by its name; the file does not define it)
fields.routes_count: number of routes serving the stop that day
fields.src: "ctan" = metropolitan consortium stop (outside the municipality); absent = the supplied city file
fields.approx: 1 = departures inferred from the neighbouring timing points (ctan only)
fields.nucleo: place within the municipality (ctan only, where known)

bus_service.caveat: A dated schedule, not live tracking or ridership. Stop departures must not be summed into unique journeys. No scheduled service on this date does not mean the stop is closed.

ctan.method: The consortium publishes each trip's times at timing points (towns or named stops), not at every stop: departures per stop are inferred. A trip counts at a stop when a timing point covering the stop (the stop itself, its place, else its municipality) has a time, or — where none covers it — when the nearest timing points before and after it on the line both have a time (approx = 1). Monday 26 Oct 2026: frequency masks starting with L, minus trips noted as Friday / Saturday / eve-of-holiday only.
limitations: 238 stops of these lines lie inside the Granada municipality and are NOT in the layer: inside the city only the supplied file (urban lines) is shown, so metropolitan departures in the city are missing.
58 stops in the consortium's general list are on no current line and are left out.
Timing points that could not be placed on a line's stop sequence: 22 of 750 (their lines fall back to the neighbouring timing points).

flow_paths.title: Terrain-derived flow paths (approximation)
flow_paths.source: Computed in this repository from IGN MDT25 (25 m) — tools/build_flow.js
flow_paths.license: CC BY 4.0 — © Instituto Geográfico Nacional (input DEM)
flow_paths.method: priority-flood depression filling, D8 flow directions, flow accumulation; lines where the upslope area is ≥ 10 ha; classes 10–50, 50–250, 250–1000, ≥ 1000 ha
flow_paths.limitations: 25 m bare-earth model: no kerbs, gutters, drains, culverts, buildings or sewer network; filled depressions can route water across real barriers; not a flood or drainage model; upslope area counts only terrain inside the 20 × 20 km DEM square, so rivers entering from outside it (e.g. the Genil) are underestimated

base_edge.title: Edge of the Base Aérea de Armilla: outline, fence classes, dead ends, walking routes, 300 m band, town points (story tour)
base_edge.source: OpenStreetMap contributors — way 130984030 (landuse=military, aeroway=aerodrome, “Base Aérea de Armilla”) and all OSM data in -3.685…-3.595 E, 37.095…37.165 N, read from the OSM API /api/0.6/map in 0.01° tiles
base_edge.method: tools/build_base_edge.py in EPSG:25830. Fence split every 25 m; each piece classed by a 35 m disc 40 m outside it: housing (OSM buildings > 8 % or landuse=residential > 40 %; industry if industrial/commercial land is larger there), industry (landuse industrial/commercial/retail > 40 %), road (motorway/trunk/primary/secondary or link within 30 m), green (parks, gardens, grass, scrub, meadow > 30 %), else open. Dead ends: degree-1 nodes of walkable highways (no motorway/trunk, no access=private|no without foot=yes, no foot=no) outside the base within 80 m of the fence. Routes: shortest paths on that network (Churriana centre −3.6463, 37.1478 → Alhendín north −3.6440, 37.1125; Las Gabias metro end −3.66567, 37.13708 → Ogíjares centre −3.6085, 37.1205). Band: outline buffered 300 m minus the outline, with OSM land use inside. Town points: OSM place nodes (Las Gabias = “Gabia Grande”).
base_edge.limitations: Only as complete as OSM: untagged land counts as open (OSM maps fields only partly); building and land-use coverage varies by street. The 1981 BOE protection limit (300 m west and south) is quoted from the brief, to be confirmed whether still in force; the band here is drawn on all sides. Wikipedia gives 369 ha for the base; 371 ha is measured on the OSM outline.

tour_area.title: Granada agglomeration by municipality: residents 2015/2025, net income per person, rent index (story tour)
tour_area.source: INE tables 2871 (Cifras oficiales de población, padrón continuo, 1 January), 31025 (Atlas de distribución de renta de los hogares, ADRH), 59060 (Índice de Precios de Vivienda en Alquiler, IPVA, municipalities over 10,000 residents), via servicios.ine.es/wstempus; outlines: npm es-atlas 0.6.0 (MIT; IGN shapefiles, CC BY 4.0); municipality list: es.wikipedia “Área metropolitana de Granada”, POTAUG list (34 municipalities, checked 2026-11-10)
tour_area.license: INE: free reuse with attribution (INE legal notice); IGN data CC BY 4.0; es-atlas code MIT
tour_area.method: tools/build_tour_area.py: change = pop2025/pop2015 − 1; groups summed from municipalities (five towns = Armilla, Churriana de la Vega, Las Gabias, Alhendín, Ogíjares). Income: net income per person, latest ADRH year in the table. Rent: IPVA index 2015 = 100, latest year.
tour_area.limitations: Rent in €/m² is missing: the MIVAU SERPAVI site refused automated download (HTTP 403) on 2026-11-10; the IPVA index measures change, not level, and exists only for 14 of the 34 municipalities. Census-section income is not mapped to neighbourhoods (no section boundaries in the atlas). es-atlas outlines are quantised to ~0.002° (~200 m). The brief named 32 municipalities; the current POTAUG list on es.wikipedia has 34 (it includes Colomera and Valderrubio, separated from Pinos Puente in 2013).

tour_towns.title: Where people live around the Base Aérea de Armilla: residential areas of the five towns (story tour)
tour_towns.source: OpenStreetMap contributors — landuse=residential areas, building footprints, admin_level=8 boundaries and place nodes in -3.705…-3.575 E, 37.085…37.175 N, read from the OSM API /api/0.6/map in 0.01° tiles on 2026-11-15; the municipal faces named with IGN, WFS unidades-administrativas (au:AdministrativeUnit); every area looked at on the PNOA orthophoto (IGN WMS pnoa-ma)
tour_towns.method: tools/build_tour_towns.py in EPSG:25830, the same for all five towns. Continuous areas (k = core at the town's OSM place node, k = part elsewhere in the municipality): residential land use plus estates without a land-use polygon (at least 8 houses, each within 24 m of the next), joined with a 40 m closing, cut at the municipal line, parts under 0.5 ha dropped. Scattered houses (k = scatter): the remaining houses in groups of at least 10, each within 100 m of the next, outlined 30 m around them (holes under 1 ha filled), pieces under 1 ha dropped. Houses = buildings tagged house, residential, apartments, detached, semidetached_house, terrace or bungalow. One place cut out by hand after the orthophoto (a retail and warehouse estate south of the Alhendín junction that OSM maps as residential). Simplified by 5 m.
tour_towns.limitations: Only inside the frame: Las Gabias (40 % of its area) and Alhendín (65 %) continue beyond it and were not looked at there. Only as complete as OSM: residential land use includes vacant plots; some houses in the scattered areas between Gabia Chica and Alhendín are not in OSM, so those outlines and house counts are lower bounds; lone farmhouses, industrial, farm and untyped buildings are not marked. The municipal line is OSM's (IGN's INSPIRE outline is generalised and differs from it by 2–17 ha per town along the borders).
